definition: A memory of past experiences that someone tells or writes about, often with fondness.
example: The old sailor's reminiscence of a storm off the coast held the whole dock silent.
nuance: A recollection can be any neutral act of remembering, but a reminiscence is usually shared aloud or lingered over with warmth.
prompt: At her retirement party, a teacher talks about her first year in the classroom.
options: Her reminiscence of that first noisy classroom drew knowing smiles.
Her reminiscence of the cruise she will take next spring filled the room with envy.
Her daughter bears a striking reminiscence to her at that age.
Guests wrapped up every reminiscence of the cake to take home.
reasons: She is fondly sharing a memory from years ago, which fits the word exactly.
A trip that has not happened yet cannot be remembered; the word looks backward.
This confuses the word with resemblance, which describes looking alike.
Leftover pieces are remnants, not shared memories of the past.

practice.prompt: Two old friends meet at a café after twenty years apart.
options: Each friend offered a careful reminiscence of the jobs they might hold in ten years.
The barista gave them a reminiscence to bring their own cups next time.
Neither friend mentioned the past, so their talk was full of reminiscence.
Over coffee, one friend's reminiscence about their old paper route made both of them grin.
reasons: Guessing about the future is prediction, the reverse of looking back.
A prompt about a future task is a reminder, not a memory of past events.
Avoiding the past entirely contradicts a conversation built on shared memories.
Telling a happy story from their shared childhood is exactly this kind of memory.
